response: As I sit here on my [birthday] alone, I'm struck by the realization that my solitary existence has taught me a valuable lesson about self-reliance. Growing up as an only child, I've had to navigate the world without the influence of siblings, and it's forced me to develop a strong sense of independence. (This has been especially true during quiet dinners with my parents, where I've had to rely on my own thoughts and feelings to fill the space.) In those moments, I've come to appreciate the depth of our bond, and the way my parents have always been there for me, even when I was struggling to find my own way. (As I've grown older, I've come to understand that this dynamic has also created a sense of weight on my shoulders - the expectation to carry the family's hopes and dreams alone, without the support of siblings to share the burden.) (It's a feeling that's both liberating and suffocating, like being trapped in a [bracket] of my own making.) (But as I look back on my life, I realize that this experience has also given me a unique perspective on solitude and family dynamics.) (In many ways, being an only child has taught me to be content with my own company, and to find strength in my own two feet, rather than relying on others to carry me through life's challenges.)
